newsitem.title: UK: New Conoco UK unit receives first acid crude cargo.
newsitem.headline: New Conoco UK unit receives first acid crude cargo.

text.p: Conoco's Killingholme refinery in northeast England will receive its first cargo of acidic crude from the North Sea's Heidrun field this week after the start-up of a new vacuum unit, a spokesman said on Monday.
Conoco spokesman Matthew Lyons said the 860,000-barrel cargo "is going to unload in the middle of the week."

The new vacuum distillation unit, which started up last month, is the first in Europe to be able to process 100 percent runs of acid crude from fields such as Heidrun, in the Norwegian North Sea, he added.
"These acidic crudes are coming from a new generation of North Sea fields...They make up six percent of current North Sea production and by the end of the decade that figure will be doubled."

Such crudes are younger in geological terms than other crudes, contain high levels of naphthenic acids, and need to be blended with other grades by most refineries because they are highly corrosive when heated, Lyons said.
Conoco holds a share of the 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) Heidrun field which is operated by Norwegian state oil company Statoil.

Installation of the new vacuum distillation unit boosted output of gas oil by nearly 40,000 tonnes per month while cutting consumption of vacuum gas oil and vacuum residual fuel oil by 85,000 and 40,000-50,000 tonnes per month respectively.
The gas oil produced has a maximum sulphur content of 0.05 percent, complying with new European environmental legislation being introduced next month.
The refinery will continue to buy some 150,000 tonnes per month of low sulphur straight-run fuel oil.
Net crude distillation capacity has been boosted by 35,000-40,000 bpd to around 220,000 bpd.
